source_control: The catalogue states at the outset that manuscript material is Indian paper unless otherwise stated. v0.2 additionally distinguishes explicitly printed material descriptors from descriptors inherited through relational phrases such as 'as in the preceding MS' and 'as in preceding MSS'.

interpretation: Material description is systematic rather than occasional: leaf count, dimensions and line density are recorded for almost the entire 79-entry corpus.
Support follows a baseline/exception information economy: Indian paper is the declared default; palm leaf and treated/special paper states are explicitly marked.

Some material attributes are encoded relationally rather than repeated locally. Keyword frequency therefore undercounts effective material attributes when catalogue entries inherit paper, size or hand from preceding entries.
MSS 77-79 form a catalogued material family because the catalogue explicitly propagates paper, size and handwriting through cross-reference.
The catalogue converts unique manuscript paper objects into portable descriptive tuples and, in some cases, into dependency relations between printed descriptions.
next_parse_requirement: Re-parse all 79 entries for relational descriptors including preceding MS, preceding MSS, same as, as above, ditto and equivalent phrases. Store source_entry, target_entry and inherited_fields separately from explicit fields.
method_warning: Exact wording and numerical typography should be checked against page images before publication quotation. Inherited attributes must be limited to the fields explicitly named by the catalogue relation; do not propagate unstated properties such as colour sequence, age or date unless independently specified.
